subject: Posterior predictive check for sequential binary outcomes

messages.author: dc6d49599b8a256f
messages.subject: Posterior predictive check for sequential binary outcomes
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about performing posterior predictive checks for binary responses. I am trying to fit a hierarchical model to choice behavior of human subjects and I am first testing parameter recovery using simulated data. Basically, I simulate N subjects, each of which produces a sequence of binary choices {y1, y2....yt} based on my model. These choices are not independent, since each choice depends on model values calculated based on previous choices. 

I understand that posterior predictive check is a recommended way to assess parameter recovery. However, I am not sure how to do this with sequential binary outcomes as observed data; for example, how to generate 50% posterior intervals and check that 50% of the binary outcomes fall into these posterior intervals? Or is there some other way to perform PPC for this type of model? 

I would greatly appreciate any comments or suggestions. Thanks!

Best,
Wanting

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Posterior predictive check for sequential binary outcomes
parts:
The sequential nature of the data isn't a problem, but we're
usually estimating continuous parameters with Stan. You can
use any kind of posterior statistic you want to do posterior
p-value checks, such as aggregated counts of subsequences. I
just did a quick overview of the Cook et al. method:

http://andrewgelman.com/2017/04/12/bayesian-posteriors-calibrated/

We need to put a lot more of this stuff in the manual. And
you can certainly do the kind of visual diagnostics that Gelman
et al. recommend in Bayesian Data Analysis.

- Bob
